title: Radiative equilibrium estimates of dust temperature and mass in high-redshift galaxies
question: Can dust temperature and mass of a high-z galaxy be derived by assuming dust radiative equilibrium, even from sparse IR data?

data.bands: Band 8 (0.73 mm), new; Band 7 and Band 6 from literature

what.value: Redshift, H140 magnitude and lensing magnification

recipe.goal: Measure Band 8 continuum flux and size
recipe.method: Gaussian fit to the continuum image with imfit
2D chi^2 minimisation in (T_d, M_d) to the three band fluxes with CMB correction
assumptions: fiducial kappa_UV = 5.0e4 cm2/g, kappa_IR,0 = 30 cm2/g, beta = 2.0

recipe.goal: Radiative-equilibrium fits for shell and homogeneous spheres
recipe.method: 1D chi^2 minimisation in M_d, T_d fixed by radiative equilibrium; Monte Carlo over R and fluxes
key_parameters: R = 0.46±0.06 arcsec from Band 7; L_UV^esc = (8.0±1.0)e43 erg/s
assumptions: Single dust temperature, uniform ISM, no scattering, optically thin IR, H0=70, Om=0.3, OL=0.7

recipe.method: 2D chi^2 minimisation in (M_d, xi_cl) with Monte Carlo errors

evidence.quote: we estimate the continuum flux density to be $1.67 \pm 0.36$ mJy

evidence.loc: 2.1 A normal, dusty star-forming galaxy, A1689zD1
evidence.quote: we obtain $L_{\rm UV}^{\rm esc}=(8.0\pm1.0)\times(9/\mu_{\rm GL})\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$

not_stated_but_needed: CLEAN parameters (threshold, mask, cell size, image size, niter)
line-free channel selection for the Band 8 continuum
exact lines of sight and imfit region
Band 7 archival project code and its reduction
grid ranges for T_d, M_d, xi_cl in chi2 search
number of Monte Carlo realizations beyond '>10,000'
bounds of xi_cl grid other than lower limit of 10^-3
missing_for_reproduction: imaging parameters beyond taper and weighting
score_reason: Analytic formulae are fully given and inputs tabulated, so the fits are reproducible from the table; the ALMA imaging details are sparse.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, tabulated fluxes and analytic equations give numeric results that can be recomputed.
